This is an important technical skill, so let's drill it. For each of these, sketch a plot of the transformation and then derive the range and the density of the new random variable:

a. Let $X\sim\text{Unif}(0,\,1)$ and consider $Y=1/X$;
a. Let $X$ have density $f_X(x)=42x^5(1-x)$ for $0<x<1$ and consider $Y=X^3$;
a. Let $X\sim\text{Exponential}(\lambda)$ and consider $Y=4X+3$;
a. Let $X$ have density $f_X(x)=\frac{1}{\theta}x^{\frac{1}{\theta}-1}$ for $0<x<1$ and some parameter $\theta>0$, and consider $Y=-\ln(X)$;
a. Let $X\sim\text{N}(0,\,1)$ and consider $Y=|X|$.
